quest.title: Prayer in Progress...
quest.description: Maki from the Grand Narukami Shrine seems to have something on her mind...

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: Ugh... who on earth is spreading this rumor?...

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: About the fortune slips at the shrine.

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: You know what fortune slips are, right? To put it simply, they are a form of astrology done by drawing lots.

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: You can reveal some simple fortunes from the wording on the slip you get.

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: If you get a good sign, great. But people usually leave the bad signs at the shrine to rid themselves of the bad fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: But... a rumor has somehow spread that if you throw the bad slips to the top of the tree, your bad luck will be dispelled by the archon.

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: Here's the funniest part: some people even think that the higher you throw it, the faster the good luck will come and the faster the bad luck will dissipate. What nonsense!

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: As the rumors got more and more outrageous, people have started throwing Mora up the tree, too!

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: It's said that if the Mora you threw gets stuck in the branches, that means that your prayer has been accepted. Not only will your wish come true, but you will also enjoy good luck for a whole year.

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: Of course not! Let's put aside whether individual prayers can be heard or not... throwing Mora is just way off. Besides, Mora all look the same, don't they?

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: Are they expecting the archon to pick up the Mora one by one to figure out who they are from?

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: I understand that they want to pray for blessings, but... throwing things up there won't get them any.

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: Besides, it all falls down once the wind kicks up.

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: I've tried to clean the tree up by myself, but I'm not very athletic. Not only did I fail to clean it up, but I got stuck for a long time and couldn't get down...

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: But I can't just leave it unattended... Traveler, could you help me go up the roof to clean up a little?

choices.text: No problem. Leave it to me.

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: Well, I'm counting on you then, Traveler. Go to the roof and clean it up, and if you get any fortune slips, please bring them to me.

choices.text: What will you do with them?

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: Well... Ms. Hotomi says that no matter what, those are the fortunes that people sought.

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: It would be inappropriate to just throw them away. So I'll put them where they belong once they are collected.

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: *sigh* If everyone had followed the rules from the beginning, we wouldn't have so much trouble...

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: Well, I'm counting on you then, Traveler. Go to the roof and clean it up, and if you get any fortune slips, please bring them to me.

choices.text: Can't we just clear the air to solve the problem?

response.speaker: Maki
response.text: There are too many people doing it now. I don't think I can convince everyone...

talks.objective: Go to the roof to clean up

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: Thank you very much. Leave the fortune slips to me and I'll hang them up in the right place.

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: Please take these as thanks for your help.

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: I understand that people are desperate to get rid of bad luck and to get good luck...

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: But I think that if they really want to solve their problems, their own actions will be more effective than fortune slips.

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: How do they expect the gods to offer help if they don't take any action themselves...

talks.objective: Go to the roof to clean up

dialogues.speaker: Maki
dialogues.text: Seriously, why do people believe in rumors that don't make sense if you just thought about them for a second?

talks.objective: Go to the roof to clean up
